newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA TRANSPORT - Technical outlook mixed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA TRANSPORT - Technical outlook mixed.

text.p: ---------------Analysis by Daniel Fock - Dec 13-------------
Shares in Brambles Industries Ltd (Thursday close A$22.05) have been bullish since their low of A$11.40 in January/February 1995.
With the market now technically overbought, traders are likely to be cautious about holding longs.
Technicals are mixed with the moving averages all bullish and the leading indicators overbought and turning lower.
Cautious traders are expected in the light of the strength of the bull run wait until both Stochastics turn down and below 80, before selling outright.
Currently the longer term is at 92/93 and medium term 79/82.
A full retracement of the longer term third wave would target A$18.32, A$17.00 and A$15.67.
However, traders are more likely to consider the shorter medium term third wave from the interim low of A$16.90 in July 1996.
On a break of support at A$21.70 traders are seen focusing on the Fibonacci retracements of A$20.42, A$19.75 and A$19.07.
Brambles is in a bull trend, but is overbought and traders will be reluctant to sell prematurely.
They are likely to wait for a break of support at A$21.70 with confirmation on a break of A$21.00 before selling.
Mayne Nickless Ltd (Thursday close A$8.20) is showing a potentially bearish head and shoulders pattern, coupled with a possible break down of the medium term bull channel.
Mayne has bounced higher from support at A$7.78, but on a break down through this level traders will most likely sell.
The technicals are bearish.
There is some bullishness only in the averages.
The leading indicators have turned lower. Some longer term traders may wait for the longer term Stochastic to move lower through 80. It is currently 77/82.
The head and shoulders pattern has a forming right shoulder at A$8.99, with the left peaking at A$8.88, and the head is at the A$10.04 high in Feb 1994.
The half right shoulder is the medium term bull channel since the low at A$5.43 in Jun 1995.
Channel support has broken, but the prices have recovered higher.
Traders are likely to be very cautious and the price must stay above A$7.78 for the bull market to continue.
While essentially bullish, Mayne has traded broadly sideways between A$$6 and A$$9 since 1991.
Having topped out at A$8.99 in October the stock may follow its pattern and retrace lower. The key level to watch is A$7.78.
Qantas Airways Ltd (Thursday close A$2.06) has continued to fall since its high of A$2.47 in March 1996.
Recently with some consolidation to just below A$2.00, coupled with a reverse head and shoulders, could see the stock up to as high as A$2.28.
The technicals are bullish, with all indicators moving higher.
The prices could stall in the short term, as short term Stochastics are overbought at 90/76.
Fibonacci retracements are A$1.99, A$1.98 and A$1.96. If this is the turn the traders have been waiting for, it is unlikely that Qantas will trade lower than A$1.99.
The reverse head and shoulder has been forming since September 1996.
Neckline resistance has co-insided with down channel resistance at A$2.02.
The prices have just moved higher and with the short term technicals overbought, traders will be cautiously bullish.
The target is A$2.28, but prices must remain above support at A$1.99 for the target to hold.
Traders are likely to be cautious buyers,looking for higher targets provided support on the stock holds.
(Daniel Fock is a member of the Australian Technical Analysts Association. Views are his own, not those of Reuters.)
